backups.name: Lefty
backups.overview: A compact, technical face/friction line on the Friction Therapy slab that needs no gear beyond quickdraws.
backups.beta: Delivers varied movement styles across a modest distance - mostly technical face climbing with clever beta and a little friction. Climbers debate whether it has a true 5.11 crux, but it feels notably harder than the adjacent line.
backups.face: Center line on the Friction Therapy slab (originally the leftmost line before another route was added further left)
backups.comms: No reliable cell service at Washington Pass; nearest dependable coverage is down-valley toward Mazama/Winthrop.
backups.descent: Lower or rappel from the bolted anchor
what_to_bring: sturdy approach shoes for the Early Winters Creek crossing
backups.pro_needs: No trad gear needed - fully bolted ('no widgets necessary').
backups.best_season: Best in summer, late June through September; the crag holds shade until early/mid-afternoon.
backups.approach: From Highway 20, park at the pullout near Mazama before the Spires Gully parking area. Descend through trees to Early Winters Creek, cross it, follow it downstream, then angle up-slope and contour left to the crag. About 20-25 minutes.
backups.descent_text: Route ends at a bolted anchor on the Friction Therapy slab; lower off or rappel with a single rope.
backups.bail: Lower off the bolted anchor at the top if needed.

pitch_detail.notes: Technical face/friction climbing on the Friction Therapy slab; fully bolted, no trad gear needed.

backups.name: Friction Therapy
backups.overview: A short, fun friction slab climb up the center rib of a distinct slab left of the crag's original JMK-established routes; first put on record in 2023.
backups.beta: Fun movement on really nice stone follows the center rib up the slab. It feels deceptively short due to concentrated difficulty, with a couple of stout (5.10+) moves in the middle.
backups.face: Right-most line on a separate slab, left of JMK's routes (identifiable by a large dead snag leaning against the wall)
backups.comms: No reliable cell service at Washington Pass; nearest dependable coverage is down-valley toward Mazama/Winthrop.
backups.descent: Lower or rappel from the bolted anchor
backups.detailed_rack: 6 bolts to a bolted anchor with rap rings; quickdraws only.
what_to_bring: sturdy approach shoes for the Early Winters Creek crossing
pro_tips: Short climbers may struggle to reach the crux clip in the middle bolt run - be ready for a reachy sequence or bring a stick clip.
backups.best_season: Best in summer, late June through September; the crag holds shade until early/mid-afternoon.
backups.approach: From Highway 20, park at the pullout near Mazama before the Spires Gully parking area. Descend through trees to Early Winters Creek, cross it, follow it downstream, then angle up-slope and contour left to the crag. About 20-25 minutes.
backups.descent_text: Route ends at a bolted anchor with rap rings; lower off or rappel with a single rope.
backups.bail: Lower off the bolted anchor at the top if needed.

backups.name: On the Prowl (D)
hazards: Loose/blocky terrain at the very start of the route
backups.overview: A quirky single pitch beginning on blocky, scrambly ground at the downhill end of the Ice Box, climbing deceptively low-angle dark rock past an exposed traverse to an arete, then a bolted leftward traverse near the top to an anchor shared with a neighboring unnamed trad line.
backups.beta: Begins on blocky terrain at the downhill (toward-the-hairpin) end of the wall. Above the scrambly start the rock looks deceptively low-angle; scramble the lower section and trend right as it steepens, aiming for the arete after a short, exposed rightward traverse. Continue up varied knobs, crimps, and jugs. Near the top, traverse left on bolts through steeper, similarly-featured climbing to the anchors — the position and quality of climbing are better than the route looks from the ground, though the bolts themselves can be hard to spot before starting.
backups.turnaround: Scope the bolt line from the ground before committing since the hardware is hard to see; if you can't confirm gear placement or the exposed low traverse feels wrong for the party, back off rather than press on.
backups.rappels: Lower from the bolted, hook-equipped anchor at the top of the wall (single pitch, 21 m).
backups.face: Ice Box right-hand wall, far right/downhill end (toward the hairpin)
backups.descent: Lower from the bolted, hook-equipped anchor at the top.
obj_haz: Short, exposed rightward traverse low on the route
Bolts are hard to spot from the ground, complicating on-lead route-finding
Blocky/loose terrain at the scrambling start

waypoints.name: Ice Box right side (base of wall)

backups.detailed_rack: 7+ quickdraws for the bolts, plus the bolted top anchor (shared with the neighboring unnamed trad line at this crag); a 60 m rope is ample for this 21 m/70 ft pitch.
what_to_bring: approach shoes for the scrambly start and 3rd-class approach
helmet — blocky terrain low on the route and in the approach gully
pro_tips: Trust the deceptively low-angle-looking rock above the scramble start — it climbs better than it looks
Scope the bolt line from the ground first, since the hardware is hard to spot
The position and rock quality make this one worth doing despite an unassuming look from below
watch_out: Route looks like nothing from below — don't underestimate the exposure once on it
Bolts can be difficult to locate visually before starting
Short, exposed rightward traverse low on the route
backups.pro_needs: Bolt-protected (~7 bolts) with a bolted, hook-equipped anchor; no natural gear needed.
backups.best_season: Same summer window as the rest of Hairpin Crags/Ice Box; best climbed in the crag's brief afternoon sun.
backups.approach: Park at the hairpin switchback on SR-20 between the Washington Pass summit and Early Winters/Mazama. Follow the climbers' trail up toward the chasm/gully right of the drainage, cross left below a slab, then scramble 3rd-class terrain up the left margin of the slabs into the Ice Box — about 15 minutes from the car. This route starts at the downhill (right-hand, toward-the-hairpin) end of the wall.
backups.descent_text: Single pitch (21 m/70 ft) — lower directly from the top bolted anchor (fitted with rap hooks) back to the base; no walk-off needed.
backups.bail: Bolt-protected (about 7 bolts); retreat at any point by lowering off a bolt.

pitch_detail.notes: Scrambly blocky start; short exposed rightward traverse to the arete; varied face climbing on knobs/crimps/jugs; final leftward bolted traverse near the top to the shared anchor.

backups.itinerary: A short afternoon outing: drive to the hairpin pullout, make the 15-minute scramble approach into the Ice Box, climb the route, then lower and walk back to the car.

access.closures: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) is gated and impassable in winter, typically early December to mid-spring.

backups.name: Iceman
backups.season: Summer — a shaded destination good for hot days when nearby Mazama crags are too warm.
hazards: Slick approach slabs pose a fall hazard on the hike in, independent of the climbing itself.
Alpine granite setting means occasional loose rock off-route.
backups.overview: A one-pitch 5.10a/b line up the shaded Ice Box (Left Side) buttress, the 'dead middle' finger-crack/roof line splitting sport routes Route C and Route D.
backups.beta: Climbs a steep face on good holds to a bolt guarding a thin finger-crack move, then finishes on horizontal cracks into an awkward but enjoyable left-facing corner. Mixed protection (3 bolts plus small-to-mid cams) makes it the trad line of the three Ice Box routes.
backups.turnaround: Start early enough to be off the exposed approach slabs and rock before afternoon thunderstorms, which are common in the North Cascades in summer; treat the slick granite slabs as more hazardous in rain.
backups.face: Ice Box (left side), Hairpin Crags — the finger-crack line between two of the sport routes
backups.comms: No cell phone service is available at Washington Pass or along this stretch of the North Cascades Highway corridor per NPS and WSDOT; do not rely on a signal for emergencies.
backups.descent: Lower or rappel from the anchor back to the base.
obj_haz: Smooth, slippery approach slabs above the dry creek bed (fall hazard, worse when wet)
Loose rock possible on unfeatured alpine granite

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Same trailhead used for the Concord/Lexington cluster; from the climber's path, cut right into a dry creek bed and ascend fixed-line slabs to the Ice Box.

waypoints.name: Ice Box Left Side Base
waypoints.note: Base of the Ice Box wall, shared by Iceman, Route C, and Route D; approach slabs are smooth and slippery.

backups.detailed_rack: 3 fixed bolts protect the crux face and finger-crack section; supplement with a small rack of cams from about BD #0.3 to #1 for the horizontal-crack and corner finish. A single 60m rope and standard quickdraws/alpine draws are sufficient for this one-pitch route.
what_to_bring: Approach shoes suited to slick granite slabs
pro_tips: Good handholds on the initial face make the opening moves easier than they look — save gear placements for after the bolt-protected finger-crack crux.
Combine with neighboring Route C and Route D for a full day at this shaded, cooler crag.
backups.watch_out:
Approach slabs above the dry creek bed are smooth and slippery, and the lower slab has no hand-line — worse when wet.
Only the crux face and finger crack are bolted; the horizontal cracks and left-facing corner above need your own small-to-mid cams.
Alpine granite can shed occasional loose rock off-route.
backups.pro_needs: Mixed protection — 3 bolts plus a handful of small-to-medium cams (0.3-1 BD equivalent) placed in the horizontal cracks and finishing corner.
backups.best_season: Late June through September, matching the broader Washington Pass climbing season; the Ice Box's shaded, north-facing character keeps it cooler than sunnier Washington Pass walls and can hold wet rock or residual snow later into the early season.
backups.approach: Spire Gully right (Alpenkuhl), part of the Hairpin Crags, is reached from the same large pullout at the hairpin turns on SR-20 near Washington Pass used for Kangaroo Temple. Looking up toward South Early Winter Spire from the pullout, Spire Gully is the obvious gully just below and left; Alpenkuhl is its sunnier, south-facing right side (the left side is known as Tiger Wall). The approach is one of the shortest at Washington Pass — a direct walk/scramble of roughly 10-15 minutes straight up from the highway, snow-covered in early season and a worn boot path later in summer.
backups.descent_text: From the top anchor, lower on a single strand or rappel with a 60m rope directly back to the base of the route; no walk-off is required for this single-pitch line.
backups.bail: Straightforward retreat on a single-pitch route — lower or rappel off the highest gear/bolt placed at any point.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep face on good holds to a bolt protecting a thin finger-crack section, then horizontal cracks into a left-facing corner finish.

backups.itinerary: A single-day cragging objective, typically combined with Route C and/or Route D at the same crag: drive to the hairpin turn on SR-20, approach via the slab/creek-bed trail, climb, then lower/rappel and retrace the approach to the car.
